title: Study on the Effect of Oxygen in Fe-Ti Hydrogen Storage Alloy with Phase and Microstructure Analysis
content: Some of the hydrogen storage alloys used include LaNi2, ZrV2, Mg2Ni, and FeTi. Fe-Ti based alloys are frequently used due to their good adsorption and desorption capability and relatively low cost. They exhibit significant variations in hydrogen storage capacity depending on the Fe/Ti ratio. According to the Fe-Ti phase diagram, there are two compound phases in the Fe-Ti binary system: FeTi and Fe2Ti. Among them, FeTi is known to have the best hydrogen storage capacity. Despite the advantages of these FeTi alloys, there is little research on how they change their properties in an oxygen atmosphere [1–3]. In this study, FeTi alloys of various compositions were fabricated and the effects of oxygen on each were investigated. Alloys with Fe60%-Ti40% were cast through arc melting furnace and heat treated in an oxygen atmosphere. Afterwards, the alloys were analyzed using SEM, EDS, and APT to investigate the effects of oxygen on the of FeTi alloys. Furthermore, multiscale analysis, on the oxide layer of FeTi alloys provide atomic scale insight on mechanism of oxidation sequence. The hydrogen permeation test was conducted to find out how those oxide layers affect the hydrogen storage capacity of FeTi alloys.
